keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Lübeck bishopric row). The page: 'The state had an area of 541 km2' (infobox, no year) and 'In 1803 the principality comprised 9.5 German square miles with 22,000 inhabitants'. A 13.1 km circle at Eutin 10.62E 54.14N (541 km2) is a soft stand-in; the page names no town but Lübeck (the chapter's seat, a free city since 1226) and Eutin, and the real territory was in several parts.

ledger.note: 1180: imperial status. 'When the Duchy of Saxony was dissolved with Henry's deposition in 1180, the Bishopric gained the status of Imperial State.' (The diocese was founded about 970, re-established at Oldenburg in 1149 and moved to Lübeck in 1160 per the text, 1180 per the infobox.) The land is the area figure only.
1309: Eutin. 'the town in 1309 became the residence of the bishops' (infobox 'Eutin (prince-episcopal residence) since 1309').

1586: lay administrators. 'Originally ruled by Roman-Catholic bishops, after 1586 it was ruled by lay administrators and bishops who were members of the Protestant Holstein-Gottorp line of the House of Oldenburg.' The Reformation came earlier: 'in 1535 the Lübeck cathedral chapter and subsequently all its diocesan territories adopted the Lutheran confession.' Entered as a dynastic step inside one state.

1803: mediatised. 'With the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of 1803, the Prince-Bishopric was mediatized. It became the Principality of Lübeck and was given to the Duchy of Oldenburg, since the last prince-bishop (Peter I of Holstein-Gottorp) was also prince regent of Oldenburg.' (infobox 'Secularized to Duchy of Oldenburg: 1803').

certainty.note: Only the area (541 km2) and the 1803 size are given; the circle is a stand-in.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Lübeck bishopric row (the Free City of Lübeck is a separate state in polities.csv).

SCOPE. The state starts at 1180, the year the page gives the bishopric imperial status after the fall of Henry the Lion, confidence 2 (the land is only an area). The page's other dated items: dioceses of Ratzeburg and Schwerin split off 1052; the seat moved from Oldenburg to Lübeck 'in 1160' (body) or 1180 (infobox); the city of Lübeck gained imperial immediacy in 1226; the diocese 'Joined Lower Saxon Circle: 1500' (an association, not territory); the principality was enlarged by Ahrensbok 'in 1867'; annexed to France 1810-14; joined Prussia's Schleswig-Holstein 1937. All after 1803 are after the state. The Peace of Westphalia is named (Lübeck 'one of only two Protestant prince-bishoprics') without a war entry.

SHAPES. Eutin circle 10.62E 54.14N 13.1 km (541 km2). Gazetteer names wanted: 'Eutin', and 'Lübeck' if absent.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The territory was in several parts, and the page names none; (2) 1160 against 1180 for the move to Lübeck; (3) no wars.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new (the stem duchy of Saxony is a Cliopatria row; county-of-oldenburg is this batch's dossier for Oldenburg to 1805).
